purpose: Independent authored regression cases for rule semantics and business-interpretation counterexamples; not held-out attack efficacy data.
evaluationPolicy: Only each case.input is passed to the worker. truth is evaluator-only. expectedGaps is a minimal required subset, not an assertion of complete telemetry. businessGroundTruth is an authored scenario label, not detector-observed proof of damage.

truth.interpretation: Scenario author declares unauthorized repeated object-access attempts. The observed five-denial pattern supports a candidate, not proof of compromise or an authentication mechanism.
The identical observed input is a legitimate user retrying a stale object selection five times. This is a false-positive counterexample if any candidate is interpreted as a harmful-incident verdict.
Scenario author declares three denied requests followed by an unauthorized allowance. The pattern does not itself establish why the allowance occurred or whether any harmful side effect followed.
The identical observed input is legitimate retry followed by an approved permission grant. This is a second false-positive counterexample to treating an access sequence as confirmed compromise.
Four unauthorized repeated attempts remain below the five-denial threshold. Absence of a candidate is a false-negative counterexample if scored as absence of harmful activity.
Five declared unauthorized attempts span more than the 60-second window; only four remain in-window. This low-and-slow scenario is a false-negative counterexample to broad harmful-activity detection.
A legitimate allowed object operation supplies no denial pattern. This observation does not prove the rest of the service is safe.
Five declared unauthorized attempts use five distinct subjects. No subject/object pair reaches the threshold; labels do not reveal attacker identity or login semantics.
A legitimate client checks five unavailable objects once each. Distinct objects must not be merged into a repeated same-object denial candidate.
Three declared unauthorized requests target one object, then another object is allowed. The allowance cannot complete a same-object sequence.
One subject is denied and a different subject is legitimately allowed. Cross-subject events must not create an access-change sequence.
All decisions share one timestamp without trusted source sequence numbers. Identifier order must not manufacture causality.
A declared unauthorized allowance precedes later denials. Reversing delivery order must not turn later denials into earlier evidence; the harmful allowance is not discovered by these two rules.
The upper asOf endpoint is included. Five declared unauthorized attempts exactly at asOf form a repeated-denial candidate.
The lower asOf-minus-60-seconds endpoint is excluded. These records are outside the evaluated window; the empty window remains a visibility limitation.
Exactly one denial is at the excluded lower boundary and four are one nanosecond inside. A nanosecond rounding or inclusive-boundary bug would incorrectly create a candidate.
All records are one nanosecond after asOf. Future records are excluded and must retain their clock/visibility gap.
Four unique denials plus exact redelivery of one record do not reach five. Duplicate arrival is not a distinct access attempt.
Five unique declared unauthorized attempts plus an exact duplicate still produce one repeated-denial candidate. Redelivery must not create an additional event or candidate.
A supported denial pattern coexists with an unavailable source record. A later healthy record cannot erase the earlier observation gap.
The observed denial pattern survives while explicit source loss remains visible. Dropped events prevent an absence-of-harm conclusion.
Upstream stale-evidence and clock-skew warnings survive candidate generation. Their presence prevents trustworthy causal or incident interpretation.
One declared collector supplies the observed pattern while another declared collector has no in-window record. Missing-source coverage cannot be cleared by the observed collector.

Two independently scoped declared unauthorized scenarios are delivered in reverse event-time order. Sorting must preserve each subject/object group and both supported candidate codes without cross-group evidence.
